dossier.public_summary: The faint 14.2-day dip shows extreme debris-depth scatter across sectors and individual transits, with only a handful of deep events making the signal. A secondary dip and grazing geometry with an inconclusive centroid and a nearby star able to mimic the dip make a planet unlikely. Together this is best explained as a false positive from a blended or systematic origin.

reasons.why: Depth changes by 283.2% between sectors (1467, 8, 538, 25, 1267, -63 ppm). sector_depths_by_source verdict is 'changes_within_a_source' with p_constant_all 1.1045244979072254e-32, so the change is real within a source, not a calibration offset.

Individual transits are inconsistent (mean 479 ppm, chi2 342.07019652273 dof 10). Top 3 transits carry share_of_top_3 0.847 of the signal and 1512 ppm outlier at 9.5 sigma shows dip is driven by few events, consistent with a systematic / false positive.
A phase 0.5769 secondary dip at 159.8 ppm is detected above best_brightening_snr 3.951, and secondary_over_bump 1.296. xenogboost planet_rank 0.06 strongly disfavours planet.

No sector with a clear difference image; 1 plausible neighbour within 1px (sep 8.1") could cause the dip with 0.0474 eclipse, and fit_b 0.9761 grazing geometry leaves a blend/EB on-target or nearby viable despite flat shape (v_sigma 0.4903).
